_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists SC as 'photo ID requested' (non-strict). SoS confirms voters without photo ID may vote a provisional ballot and return with photo ID within 48 hours, or sign an affidavit with a reasonable impediment. Consistent. 2026-06-10 verification (scvotes.gov 2026prep): primary June 9, 2026 CONFIRMED (held yesterday) and runoff June 23, 2026 CONFIRMED for contests where no candidate won a majority. Early-voting windows corrected per SEC: statewide primaries May 26-June 5 (file previously ended June 6); runoff early voting is Wednesday June 17 through Friday June 19 (file previously had June 9-20); general early voting Oct 19-31 excluding Sundays.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting for the statewide primaries ran Tuesday, May 26 through Friday, June 5 (excluding Sunday), 8:30 a.m.-5 p.m. at county early voting centers.

Early voting for the June 23 runoff runs Wednesday, June 17 through Friday, June 19, 8:30 a.m.-5 p.m. at county early voting centers. If you voted in one party's primary, you may only vote in that party's runoff.
Early voting for the general election runs the two weeks before Election Day (October 19-31, excluding Sundays) at county early voting centers.
In-person absentee (early voting) is available at county election offices beginning about two weeks before Election Day.

acceptedIds: South Carolina Voter Registration Card with photo
Employee badge or ID card issued by a state or federal government agency
Student photo ID from a South Carolina public college or university
votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID must be current (not expired).
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without acceptable photo ID may cast a provisional ballot and either present ID within 2 business days, or sign an affidavit stating a reasonable impediment to obtaining photo ID.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: South Carolina prohibits use of wireless communication devices in the voting booth. You may not photograph your ballot.
additionalRules: Open primary: any registered voter may choose which party's primary to participate in.
Runoff rule: if no candidate receives a majority in the primary, the top two advance to a runoff. A voter who voted in one party's primary may only vote in that party's runoff.

eligibility: Will be absent from the county on Election Day

Workers required at workplace all polling hours
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the county board 4 days before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county board by 7 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Absentee ballot must arrive at the county board by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: South Carolina rule: if you voted in one party's primary, you can only vote in that same party's runoff. If you did not vote in the primary, you may choose either party's runoff.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: South Carolina has an open primary with no party registration (S.C. Code Ann. §7-11-10). Any qualified voter may participate in any party's primary by signing a pledge to support the nominees. If a runoff occurs, you must vote in the same party's runoff as the primary you participated in.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Carolina del Sur tiene una primaria abierta sin registro de partido (S.C. Code Ann. §7-11-10). Cualquier votante calificado puede participar en la primaria de cualquier partido firmando un compromiso de apoyar a los nominados. Si hay una segunda vuelta, debe votar en la segunda vuelta del mismo partido en cuya primaria participó.
